sections.title: Headline
sections.content: AI-native developer infrastructure dominates today's list: code review, local model inference, research agents, and multi-agent source control all appear among the fastest-growing repositories. The strongest individual gain is VoiceStudio, while colibri shows unusually strong interest in running frontier MoE models on commodity hardware.

sections.title: alibaba/open-code-review
sections.description: Hybrid, agent-assisted code review at Alibaba scale.

sections.title: JustVugg/colibri
sections.description: A zero-dependency C engine for running frontier MoE models from disk.

sections.title: ever-co/ever-gauzy
sections.description: Open business-management software spanning ERP, CRM, HRM, ATS, and project management.

sections.title: debpalash/VoiceStudio
sections.description: A fully local voice-cloning, dubbing, transcription, and audiobook toolkit.

sections.title: melgarafael/DeskcommCRM
sections.description: Self-hosted AI sales CRM with WhatsApp integration and MCP support.

sections.title: alphaXiv/OpenResearch
sections.description: Tools for turning coding agents into research agents.

sections.title: danny-avila/LibreChat
sections.description: Self-hosted ChatGPT-style platform with agents, MCP, model switching, and integrations.

sections.title: pacifio/atlas
sections.description: Source control and coordination for multiple coding agents.

sections.title: Trending Technologies and Themes
sections.content: Agent-native developer tooling; local and private AI; AI entering established workflows; TypeScript leads with 3 repositories, Rust has 2, and Go, C, Python, Swift, and Java each have 1.

sections.title: Notable Shifts
sections.content: The clearest shift is from standalone AI demos toward operational infrastructure: review pipelines, agent source control, research loops, self-hosted chat, and business software.

sections.title: Takeaway
sections.content: Today's list points to an AI tooling market moving up the stack. The most visible opportunities are the control planes, integrations, and local runtimes that make agents useful inside real engineering and business workflows.
